newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia targets fiscal deficit in '98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Colombia targets fiscal deficit in '98 budget.

text.p: Colombia will endeavor to cut the central government's fiscal deficit, which is expected to rise to 4.8 percent of gross domestic product this year, as part of its 1998 spending program, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Friday.

He spoke after a meeting of the National Council for Economic and Social Policy (CONPES), where he and other senior officials approved a preliminary 1998 budget totalling 29.9 trillion pesos, up 14.2 percent over 1997.

Ocampo stressed that the budget forecast included the government's financing needs for debt service, however, and said that without funds earmarked for debt payments it totalled 23.2 trillion pesos against 25.8 trillion in 1997.
"This reflects the austerity effort (that is being made) and shows the fiscal commitment of the government," he said. "The budget approved by the (council) is austere," he added.

In his remarks to reporters, Ocampo initially said that the central government's fiscal deficit would be cut to 4.5 percent of GDP in 1998. But he later revised that figure to say the deficit would be trimmed to 4.3 percent of GDP.
Colombia began 1997 with a federal deficit of about 4.0 percent, one of the highest of any major country in the region.

Ocampo did not detail how it would be cut back in 1998, which is an election year in Colombia and a time when the ruling Liberal Party will be hard pressed to cut social spending. But he said the country's overall deficit stood at 2.4 percent of GDP and vowed that this would drop to 2.1 percent next year.
Ocampo also reiterated his earlier forecasts for GDP growth of at least 3.0 percent this year and 4.5 percent in 1998.
